property_summary: After a successful initialize(accessControl), access-guarded functions like setSlopes must succeed when accessControl grants access; the mutant never stores accessControl (address(0)), so setSlopes always reverts with AccessDenied.

For every caller and access-control address, initialize() can advance the initialized version at most once: any subsequent initialize() call must revert with InvalidInitialization; the mutant removes the version latch ($._initialized = 1), so it re-enters initialSetup and lets initialize() succeed repeatedly.

For any access-control address, a fresh C must allow exactly one top-level initialize(...) call to complete successfully (the initializer sets _initializing so nested onlyInitializing init steps run), but the mutant never sets the flag so initialize always reverts with NotInitializing.

A fresh contract context may call initialize twice during its own construction (code.length == 0), because the initializer's construction path accepts version 1; the mutant records version 2 after the first call, so the second construction-time initialize reverts, breaking the rule that a double construction-time initialization always succeeds.
